newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli and Egyptian presidents to meet on peace.
newsitem.headline: Israeli and Egyptian presidents to meet on peace.

text.p: Israel's President Ezer Weizman and Egypt's President Hosni Mubarak will meet soon to try to salvage Israeli-PLO peace talks deadlocked for the last two months, an Israeli official said on Thursday.

"There was a conversation yesterday initiated by the president of Egypt, Mubarak, and the president of Israel, Ezer Weizman, and concerning the details and as for the date of the meeting, nothing has been set as yet," Arye Shumer, director-general of Weizman's office, told Israel Radio. "I imagine we are speaking of the coming days."
Shumer said the Egyptian leader proposed the meeting during a phone call. Weizman had immediately informed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of the initiative, Shumer said.

Differences over Netanyahu's Jewish settlements policy have stalled Israeli-Palestinian peacemaking. Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat on Wednesday urged the United States to put pressure on Israel to save the process.

Weizman was an architect of Israel's landmark peace treaty with Egypt as a cabinet minister in 1979 but his job as president is largely ceremonial and his current peace efforts, including meetings with Arafat, have underscored the crisis Netanyahu, head of a right-wing government, has faced in peacemaking.

Israeli government spokesman Moshe Fogel, asked about the Weizman-Mubarak meeting, told Reuters without elaborating: "The prime minister's office is aware of the proposal and it's aware of the potential initiative and it's aware of what's on the table."
